notes:
PASS on the fake backend only; evidence is contract_checked, never an MHS-Device level. This package is model-authored and unreviewed (driver.lock.json reviewed_by is null); RosDriver refuses every hardware backend without a human hardware review regardless of risk, and no ROS graph, ros2_track_imu node, serial port, TrackIMU board or hardware run was used or is claimed. No preflight section for this exact package and pin was present in the two named ros-wave-b PREFLIGHT.md files.

It is a configuration-only ROS 2 RosDriver over rosbridge, mode hardware, risk R0, device_kind sensor.imu; there is no Python native class and no native.py. The pinned interface is the relative 'imu' publisher of sensor_msgs.msg.Imu (ros2_track_imu/driver.py:20, import at :3). The package configures the default root-namespace endpoint /imu and keeps source_name 'imu'; a deployment that starts the node under another namespace must expose the resolved endpoint. The node also publishes DiagnosticArray on the relative 'diagnostics' topic (driver.py:22); that observation is not bound. The node exposes no actuation, stop or reset service, and this package binds only its observation topic; no Limit is declared because the only input is the catalogue's frame enum, and no site-limits.example.json is needed. The software-only e-stop is the stock read-only behavior: the SDK latches and records safe_state_achieved true because there is no actuating capability; this is not a native or physical stop claim, and the catalogue-confirmed read remains usable during the latch.

The primary upstream limitation is that publish_imu_data assigns the orientation quaternion but the linear_acceleration and angular_velocity assignment lines are commented out (driver.py:179-187), so those message fields are the Imu defaults, i.e. zero vectors. The driver returns the class-required three-element arrays from those zero wire values; it does not claim measured accelerometer or gyro data, and acceleration/angular-velocity measurement is NOT COVERED in practice. Only the orientation is computed from the serial AHRS line. The class's frame input is honoured in the adapter: body returns the message vectors unchanged and world rotates them by the reported orientation quaternion; sampled_at is the message header stamp converted to RFC 3339, and a missing or malformed stamp, vector, orientation or non-finite value fails with MHS.CAPABILITY.OUTPUT_INVALID. The class output does not carry the header frame_id or the covariance matrices; the operator configures the node's frame_id parameter. The serial port, baud, board calibration writes (configure_imu is commented out at imu_node.py:56-60), node lifecycle, ROS graph, QoS, remapping, parameter services, diagnostics and message age are outside this package.

The fake is a ROS-free event-driven RecordingRosTransport (F0): it answers the declared /imu subscribe with a sensor_msgs/msg/Imu-shaped message and runs no serial loop, AHRS computation, wall-clock pacing, ROS node or simulator; every canned value and negative switch is a placeholder. Negative cases cover a silent topic, an unrelated event id, a broken subscription link and malformed or missing fields. No G4.REF_VALUE or G4.REF_BINARY warning remains; the only warning is G8.SAFE014_NOT_APPLICABLE, expected because a read-only sensor declares no numeric actuation limit (every other CL3 test passed). test_driver.py has nine cases: the stock gate plus the IMU output arrays and stamp, wire endpoint and type, world-frame rotation, silent timeout, unrelated id, broken subscription, malformed messages and the stock software-only e-stop with the catalogue-read exemption. The clone was left unmodified (G1 passed); no network, pip install or upstream execution was used.

MODEL REVIEW (claude-opus-5-5, a model and not a human, 2026-11-05; reviewed_by stays null): Checked the /imu subscription against the relative 'imu' Imu publisher of node 'track_imu_driver' (ros2_track_imu/driver.py:15-20, import at :3; no namespace anywhere in the clone), the cap.sensing.imu.v1 mapping with its refusal of missing, nonfinite and malformed fields, the fake's ROS 2 stamp and covariance content, the software-only e-stop of this passive R0 sensor, the provenance and all 21 facts. Five facts claimed more than their lines: a 'so ... default zero vectors' inference on 179-187, 'the launch files' citing one file, 'they configure the board' although configure_imu is commented out in main, an index-free 'assigns all four orientation components', and a covariance clause whose orientation comment starts at line 30; the reviewer narrowed or re-ranged them and added two facts, the euler2quat import alias (line 9) and that the local roll, pitch and yaw are bound only for lines with more than two fields (163-189). Reviewer changed driver.py (facts, plus a docstring and action-description caution on the quaternion component order) and facts.md, and regenerated reference.json, REFERENCE.md and check-report.json; the gate and collect.py --strict pass with the digest unchanged. For the human reviewer: Passive serial AHRS publisher; only the orientation is computed, linear acceleration and angular velocity are always zero. The node copies transforms3d euler2quat's q[0..3] into orientation x, y, z, w, while transforms3d (outside the clone) documents w-first quaternions, so the published orientation is probably permuted; the package passes it through. A serial line with two or fewer fields, including the empty line readline returns after its 1 s timeout, reaches euler2quat with unbound locals and ends the node (the main loop has no handler); reads then time out. The README's 'ros2 run ros2_track_imu imu_node' does not match setup.py's console script name ros2_track_imu.
